title: Module 5 intro — Cognition, Planning, and Memory

lines: Welcome to Module Five: Cognition, Planning, and Memory.
How an agent thinks, plans, and remembers.
Picture a research agent that writes a competitor report every Monday.
Five rivals, their prices, and a one-page summary.
In week one, it thinks hard about everything.
Slow, expensive reasoning, just to copy one price.
It never makes a plan, either.
It wanders from source to source, and the report takes forty minutes.
Then one pricing page goes offline.
The agent retries the same dead link until its budget runs out.
And every Monday, it starts from zero.
The team has said it five times: prices in euros, one page.
Fix one: route reasoning effort like any other decision.
Easy steps get a direct answer, and only hard ones get the expensive techniques.
Fix two: a planner splits the report into small, checkable steps.
The five lookups run in parallel, then feed the summary.
When a step keeps failing, the agent replans and tries another source.
After a set number of replans, it asks a human.
Fix three: memory that outlasts the session.
Preferences are stored as facts, last week's dead link as an episode, and the steps that worked as a skill.
Now the report takes eight minutes, at a fraction of the cost.
It arrives in euros, and nobody repeats themselves.
Lesson one compares six reasoning techniques, from chain of thought to tree of thoughts, and what each costs.
Sometimes the right answer is no scaffold at all.
Lesson two covers planning: right-sized steps, laid out as a dependency graph.
You'll learn what should trigger a replan, and why replanning needs a limit.
Lesson three names four memory types: working, semantic, episodic, and procedural.
The current context, durable facts, past events, and learned how-to.
Saving everything backfires, so memory needs a write policy and a way to forget.
And attackers can plant hidden instructions there.
This domain is ten percent of the exam, and questions often hinge on one phrase.
Learn the phrase that gives each technique away, starting in lesson one.
